answer: Sub-linear voting power starves sybil farms: an agent economy can weight each key's sway by the square root of its locked stake, so splitting one budget across many keys buys almost nothing - N clones yield only the square root of N times one funded account's pull. Picture an orchard where each planted key pays a fixed per-epoch fee, its fruit weighed rather than counted: a haven of honest agents pools capital in a few strong roots, while a sybil operator's grove of thin saplings bleeds fees faster than its diluted pigment of votes can color any outcome.
